title: Tales of the Texas Rangers
paragraphs: Joel McCrea stars as Texas Ranger Jace Pearson in police-style Western cases inspired by Texas law-enforcement files, combining modern investigation with the setting and traditions of the Rangers.
Modern police-procedural Western centered on fictional Texas Ranger Jace Pearson; cases were framed as dramatizations of actual Texas Ranger files/cases.

GRH documents the program through Audition (April 13, 1950 to April 13, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], NBC Wheaties launch era (July 8, 1950 to August 26, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and NBC sustaining era (September 2, 1950 to September 14, 1952) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|joel-mccrea|Joel McCrea]] (performer on 81 recordings), M. T. Lone Wolf Gonzaullas (technical advisor on 57 recordings, consultant on 22 recordings, and performer on 2 recordings), Stacy Keach (director on 81 recordings, producer on 81 recordings, and commercial spokesman on 1 recording), Hal Gibney (announcer on 79 recordings and host on 1 recording), Monty Fraser (sound-effects artist on 80 recordings), Tony Barrett (performer on 80 recordings, radio adaptor on 1 recording, and writer on 1 recording), and Joel Murcott (chief writer on 40 recordings, performer on 40 recordings, writer on 12 recordings, radio adaptor on 2 recordings, and commercial spokesman on 1 recording).

plain_text:
Joel McCrea stars as Texas Ranger Jace Pearson in police-style Western cases inspired by Texas law-enforcement files, combining modern investigation with the setting and traditions of the Rangers.

Modern police-procedural Western centered on fictional Texas Ranger Jace Pearson; cases were framed as dramatizations of actual Texas Ranger files/cases.

GRH documents the program through Audition (April 13, 1950 to April 13, 1950) on NBC Radio Network, NBC Wheaties launch era (July 8, 1950 to August 26, 1950) on NBC Radio Network, and NBC sustaining era (September 2, 1950 to September 14, 1952) on NBC Radio Network.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Joel McCrea (performer on 81 recordings), M. T. Lone Wolf Gonzaullas (technical advisor on 57 recordings, consultant on 22 recordings, and performer on 2 recordings), Stacy Keach (director on 81 recordings, producer on 81 recordings, and commercial spokesman on 1 recording), Hal Gibney (announcer on 79 recordings and host on 1 recording), Monty Fraser (sound-effects artist on 80 recordings), Tony Barrett (performer on 80 recordings, radio adaptor on 1 recording, and writer on 1 recording), and Joel Murcott (chief writer on 40 recordings, performer on 40 recordings, writer on 12 recordings, radio adaptor on 2 recordings, and commercial spokesman on 1 recording).

The program is also connected in the archive to NBC Radio Network (broadcast on network) and Armed Forces Radio and Television Service (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder and homicide, law enforcement, robbery and theft, forensic investigation, ranching and cattle, and narcotics crime.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Texas Rangers institutional cooperation, Modern forensic police-procedural framing, and Wheaties-sponsored launch.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include Lux Radio Theatre (74 shared credited people), Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar (67 shared credited people), Escape (63 shared credited people), The Whistler (60 shared credited people), and Broadway Is My Beat (51 shared credited people).
